## LMARS (`type: lmars`) {#sec-ch04-lmars}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- A low-Mach approximate Riemann solver: one face velocity and one face pressure, then a pure upwind of the state.
- Switch: `type: lmars`. It is what the shipped example decks select, though not the YAML default.
- Consistent: equal left and right states give the exact physical flux.
- Writes a face pressure, so it works with the curved-grid pressure force and the well-balanced path.
- The species rows and a dry row split the mass flux exactly.
:::

LMARS replaces the full wave structure of a Riemann problem with two numbers: an acoustically-corrected face
velocity and an acoustically-corrected face pressure. The sign of the face velocity then decides which side the
rest of the state is taken from. The result is cheap, robust at low Mach number, and the production choice in
every shipped deck.

### Derivation

Let $\bar\rho$ be the arithmetic mean density and $\bar c$ the mean sound speed built from the mean pressure.
The face velocity and pressure are

$$
\bar u = \tfrac12(u_L + u_R) + \frac{p_L - p_R}{2\bar\rho\bar c},\qquad
\bar p = \tfrac12(p_L + p_R) + \tfrac12\bar\rho\bar c\,(u_L - u_R).
$$ {#eq-ch04-lmars-face}

Each is a centred average plus an acoustic correction proportional to the jump in the *other* variable, with
$\bar\rho\bar c$ the acoustic impedance. `[C6]` checks both halves separately: a pure pressure jump of $0.2$
with no velocity jump drives $\bar u = -0.080582$, which is exactly the second term of @eq-ch04-lmars-face, and
two states converging at $0.3$ raise $\bar p$ to $1.354965$ above the mean of $1.0$, which is exactly the
impedance times the velocity jump.

Consistency follows immediately and `[C5]` checks it: with $w_L = w_R$ both jump terms vanish, so $\bar u = u$
and $\bar p = p$, and the returned flux agrees with the exact physical flux to $8.9\times10^{-16}$. That is the
property that makes the scheme usable at all; a solver that fails it would generate flux from a uniform state.

The mass rows are the part most easily misread. The dry row does not carry the total mass flux: it carries
$\bar u\rho\,r_d$ with $r_d = 1 - \sum_n y_n$, and each species row carries $\bar u\rho y_n$. `[C7]` confirms
the split is exact, with the dry row and three species rows summing to $\bar u\rho$ to $1.1\times10^{-16}$.
A reader who takes the first mass row for the total mass flux will be wrong by the species fraction.

### Numerical method

The body is [`lmars_impl.h:17-78`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/lmars_impl.h#L17-L78). It computes the enthalpies of both sides first, at
`wli` ([`lmars_impl.h:28-31`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/lmars_impl.h#L28-L31)), adding the kinetic term and $p/\rho$ to the internal enthalpy the caller
passed; then the means and @eq-ch04-lmars-face at [`lmars_impl.h:34-43`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/lmars_impl.h#L34-L43); then branches on the sign
of $\bar u$ and fills every row from the upwind side at [`lmars_impl.h:47-77`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/lmars_impl.h#L47-L77).

The face pressure is written out at `face_pressure` ([`lmars_impl.h:40`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/lmars_impl.h#L40)) when the caller asked for one, and it is
the same $\bar p$ that enters the normal momentum row, so the pressure force the geometric source sees and the
pressure in the flux are the same number by construction.

The upwind branch is on $\bar u$, which already contains the acoustic correction. At low Mach number that
correction is what decides the branch when the centred velocity is near zero, which is the mechanism behind the
scheme's low-Mach behaviour: the pressure jump, not the velocity, selects the side.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The mean sound speed is built from the arithmetic mean of the two pressures and densities. Across a strong
  jump that mean is not a physical sound speed on either side, and no source in the repository bounds the error
  that follows.
:::

1. **No entropy fix and no wave structure.** Everything that is not the acoustic correction is pure upwinding,
   so a strong expansion is resolved by the flux limiter and the floors rather than by the solver.
2. **Hypothesis, untested here.** That the acoustic correction is what gives the scheme its low-Mach behaviour
   is an argument from @eq-ch04-lmars-face, not a measurement; no deck in the repository measures a Mach-number
   scaling of the dissipation.
